candidate.blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort, printed p.11/PDF p.15: Assist with nutrition and oral hydration; Provide care related to feeding and enteral tubes
candidate.blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — enteral-feeding tolerance and tube-feeding management
candidate.educational_objective: Interpret gastric residual volume together with the client's clinical signs of enteral-feeding intolerance rather than using an isolated sub-500-mL value as an automatic stop criterion.

options.A: A residual volume below 500 mL without other signs of intolerance should not by itself trigger stopping enteral nutrition; assess tolerance and follow agency policy.
options.B: Any gastric residual above 200 mL requires permanent discontinuation of enteral nutrition regardless of the client's clinical status.
options.C: The feeding rate should be doubled immediately to clear the residual volume more quickly.
options.D: Gastric residual volume is the only valid measure of enteral-feeding tolerance, so other gastrointestinal findings are unnecessary.

candidate.rationale: Open RN Nursing Fundamentals states that although gastric residual volumes of 200-500 mL have historically prompted interventions, current evidence does not support stopping enteral nutrition for GRVs less than 500 mL when there are no other signs of intolerance. Nurses should assess for symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, bloating, cramping, diarrhea, or constipation and follow agency policy. Therefore A is correct; the other options overstate or misuse the residual-volume finding.
candidate.source_claim_supported: An isolated gastric residual volume below 500 mL without other signs of feeding intolerance should not automatically prompt stopping enteral nutrition; clinical tolerance and agency policy should guide management.
candidate.source_locator: Chapter 14 > enteral nutrition/aspiration-risk section: do not stop enteral nutrition for GRVs less than 500 mL in absence of other intolerance signs; follow agency policy; monitor for bloating, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, cramping, constipation

candidate.stem: A client receiving gastric enteral nutrition has a gastric residual volume of 350 mL and no nausea, vomiting, abdominal distention, or other signs of feeding intolerance. Which nursing interpretation is most appropriate?
